title: Self-Sustaining Life System
hook: If it only works when you remember to do it, it's not a system yet.
statement: The best systems keep running without you pushing them every single day.
explainer: Willpower and memory run out fast, especially in busy weeks. The stuff that's automated and set up right keeps going even when your head is somewhere else.
sop: List the systems held together only by your memory and willpower.
Score Automation, Alignment, and Consistency from 1 to 10 for the biggest one.
Automate the piece that's still 100% manual, like bills or reporting.
Make the right choice the default so it doesn't need willpower.
Check it monthly. Maintenance, not babysitting.
equation_example: Automation 7, Alignment 8, Consistency 6. 7 × 8 × 6 = 336. Higher means it runs right even on weeks you're not looking. Lower means it quietly stops the second your attention moves.
question: Pick one system you'd love to never think about again, and write its first automation step.
closing_statement: Build systems that survive the weeks you forget them.
caption:
Principle Nº 189: Self-Sustaining Life System

If it only works when you remember to do it, it's not a system yet.

The best systems keep running without you pushing them every single day.

Your turn: Pick one system you'd love to never think about again, and write its first automation step.
